We have applied template 20810 and got a tuple of precursor SMILES: ('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1', 'O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F'). So first reaction splits target into two fragments: a sulfonyl chloride aromatic with F? Actually O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F (para-fluoro phenyl sulfonyl chloride). The other fragment is a protected amine with t-butyl carbamate? Actually CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(...). Good.

Now we need to continue retrosynthesis using the given templates in order: after 20810, then 2895, then 1914397, 1914398, 1914399, 74054. So total 6 reactions. We have first reaction done. Next we need to apply template 2895 to each of the precursors? Probably sequentially to break down further. The route must have at least 6 reactions, using those templates in order. So we need to create a tree where each reaction uses the next template on a chosen molecule.

We need to decide which precursor to further dissect with template 2895. Likely the sulfonyl chloride can be made from something else using 2895. Or the protected amine can be further broken.

We need to check applicability of template 2895 to each precursor. Let's test on sulfonyl chloride.
